# Pinned MOBI/KF8 parser

`mobi.js` comes from John Factotum's foliate-js, official upstream commit
`78914aef4466eb960965702401634c2cb348e9b1` (reviewed 2026-10-23):
https://github.com/johnfactotum/foliate-js/blob/78914aef4466eb960965702401634c2cb348e9b1/mobi.js

Upstream documents MOBI and KF8/AZW3 support; it has no stable release and recommends pinning source. MIT license is preserved in `LICENSE`.

The Shelf changes are deliberately small and local: optional `textOnly` mode skips DOM navigation, TOC and publisher page-spread processing; DOMParser/XMLSerializer construction becomes optional; metadata entity decoding falls back to the unchanged string without a DOM; sections expose a raw `text()` method; optional EXTH fields tolerate absence; suppressed navigation warnings in text-only mode. No upstream rendering, resource replacement, URL creation, font decoding, media, or link resolution is used. The parser runs in a dedicated Worker, terminated on completion, error, page exit or 15s timeout. Book bytes never leave the browser.

`archive.mjs` rejects DRM encryption on every embedded MOBI header before decoding. Only uncompressed and PalmDOC compression are accepted; HUFF/CDIC, KFX, Topaz, encrypted Kindle and malformed/unsupported variants require a lawful local conversion. AZW suffix alone never establishes format. Existing EPUBs with encryption.xml (including font obfuscation) are refused conservatively.

This initial renderer is text-first: publisher CSS, images, fonts, links, active media and fixed-layout fidelity are omitted. Chapters become the TOC and previous/next controls navigate chapters; the chapter position persists locally. PDF uses the existing PDF.js renderer. Rendering text passes through a separate opaque, nonce-script-only CSP sandbox; it reconstructs allowlisted semantic elements with escaped text and no attributes. Display uses a second iframe with empty sandbox, `default-src 'none'`, `script-src 'none'`, no images, fonts, forms or base URL; only application-generated style is allowed. No publisher bytes are interpolated into scripts.

Limits: 20,000,000 input bytes; 2,048 archive/PDB records; 2,000,000 bytes per archive/PDB record; 32,000,000 advertised ZIP expanded bytes; streaming inflate cannot exceed advertised size or per-entry cap; 16,000,000 Kindle text bytes (conservative 8x PalmDOC preflight); 1,024 chapters; 100,000 DOM nodes, depth 64, 24,000,000 sanitized output characters. Files outside these limits fail clearly. EPUB binary work runs in the Worker too. Synthetic original fixtures and binary parser tests are in `tests/ebook-reader.test.mjs`; `node scripts/ebook-browser-fixture.mjs` provides the actual browser fixture and has no private/API access.

Allocation hardening after review: all FDST counts must fit the actual record and be <=2,048 before a table is built. INDX record counts fit the PDB/IDXT data and total index entries are <=1,024; TAGX descriptors are <=64, control bytes <=16, each scalar group <=1,024 and total values <=65,536, with <=4,096 CNCX strings and <=64 CNCX records. Varints must terminate within four available bytes; value-byte counts must fit the entry buffer and <=4,096. EXTH metadata counts/lengths must fit the record, with <=1,024 entries. Every text record is bounded by its <=4,096-byte declared size during PalmDOC expansion, before accumulating output. MOBI chapter matches are bounded before array materialization and unused file-position indexing is skipped in text-only mode. KF8 skeleton/fragment counts, insertion positions, cumulative sizes, FDST ranges and raw reads are checked before concatenation, and raw reads cannot advance beyond declared text records. These checks reject malformed/oversized structures before allocation; the Worker deadline is an additional limit, not the memory protection.
